card.summary: H.R. 9693, titled the Patients First Act of 2026, makes multiple changes to how physicians and health care practitioners are paid under the Medicare program. The bill creates a temporary hybrid payment model for certain primary care services, renames and restructures the Merit-based Incentive Payment System (MIPS) into the Patient Outcome Improvement National Tabulation System (POINTS), adjusts how annual fee schedule updates and budget neutrality thresholds are calculated, and changes data collection and reporting requirements for imaging services and clinical data registries.

card.title: Provider Reimbursement Stability Act of 2026

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: The Provider Reimbursement Stability Act of 2026 makes changes to how annual adjustments and payments are managed under the Medicare physician fee schedule. It raises the threshold for budget neutrality adjustments, requires corrections when actual service usage differs from estimated usage for certain bundled or separate services, mandates regular updates to direct cost inputs at least every five years, and places a limit on how much a conversion factor may vary from year to year.

affected_groups.effect: They experience changes to how annual fee schedule adjustments and payment rates are calculated, updated, and capped year-over-year.
The agency is required to implement higher adjustment thresholds, conduct utilization reconciliations, update direct cost prices every five years, and enforce a 2.5% variance limit.

key_provisions: Raises the annual budget neutrality adjustment difference threshold from $20 million to $57.64 million starting in 2028, with indexing every five years beginning in 2033.
Requires CMS to determine differences between estimated and actual service utilization for certain bundled or separately paid services starting in 2029.
Directs CMS to reconcile utilization differences by adjusting payments for the following year if the difference exceeds 0.1 percent of total estimated expenditures.
Mandates that CMS update direct cost inputs—such as clinical staff wage rates, medical supply prices, and equipment prices—at least once every five years simultaneously across all categories.
Prohibits CMS from varying a specific budget neutrality adjustment factor by more than 2.5% each year starting in 2028.
missing_information: The total financial cost or budgetary impact of raising thresholds and changing adjustment rules is not provided.
Specific details on how stakeholder consultations will be executed are absent.
